title: A machine for the grammar-checking stage
statement: For every machine format $F$, there exist a natural number $m$, a finite state set $S$ with decidable equality, a deterministic Turing machine $G$ with $m$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet, an entry state, an injective assignment of exit states to Boolean values, a natural number $a$, and a designated work-tape index $header$. For every input $x$ that parses as $bits$ and $rest$, with $bits$ the canonical binary representation of its value and $|rest|\ge \max\{guard,(4k+5)3^{k+1}\}(v+1)$, where $k$ is the work-tape count of $F$ and $v$ is the value of $bits$, and for every configuration $d$ on input $x$ whose state is the entry state, output is empty, input-head position is $2|bits|+3$, designated tape contains $bits$ with its head at zero, and all other tapes are blank with heads at zero, there is a time $t\le a(|x|+1)^a$ such that $G$ has empty output and is in the exit state assigned to whether the grammar check succeeds. No exit state is visited before time $t$.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of a tape count $m$, finite state set $S$ with decidable equality, machine $G$, entry state, injective Boolean exit assignment, time constant $a$, and designated tape index
The bit string $bits$ is canonical for its binary value
The suffix satisfies the specified guard bound
The initial configuration has the specified state, empty output, input-head position, designated tape contents and head, and blank contents and zero heads on other tapes
The reached state indicates success of the grammar check, output remains empty, and no exit state was visited earlier
